transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-08
Time: 10:00 AM UTC
Duration: ~45 min
Attendees: Claire Nguyen (Redwood AE), Marco Rios (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (CTO, Nexus Labs), Samira Patel (Head of ML, Nexus), Devon Price (Infra, Nexus)

Summary:
Weekly POC sync to review latest bench marks vs their baseline provider (CloudX). Focus on latency P95/P99, sustained throughput, and tuning items (batching, KV cache, quantization). Discussed next steps: share CSVs, run staging load test, schedule VPC deep dive.

Transcript:
[00:00] Claire: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check — audio's good?
[00:08] Jordan: Yeah, good here. Sorry team, timezone fun.
[00:12] Claire: No worries. Marco and I will go over the benchmark slide and the raw CSVs we uploaded. We ran the same workload you ran on CloudX last week and wanted to call out differences.
[00:28] Marco: Quick note, some of the numbers from our side, we ran with Redwood dedicated profile q4 (quantized 4-bit) and the KV cache enabled for prefix reuse. That gave us pretty consistent token latency improvements on the tail.
[00:45] Samira: When you say KV cache, do you mean the prefix caching? Sometimes the docs say K V cache, I'm just making sure it's the same thing.
[00:51] Marco: Yes, prefix/K-V cache, same. The transcriber might write it weird but it's the same.
[00:55] Devon: Also calling out our baseline on CloudX used a different micro-batching setting — they were doing 8 tokens batch and 2 concurrent streams, so we want apples-to-apples there.
[01:08] Claire: Right, we tried to match the request pattern you provided — same prompt set and concurrency. There are two big deltas we saw: first, P95 latency is about 18% lower on Redwood in our runs; second, throughput sustained (requests/sec) was comparable, sometimes slightly higher on CloudX depending on quantization.
[01:28] Jordan: Can you break down the P99? That's the one our product team worries about.
[01:34] Marco: P99 moved a bit more — on CloudX baseline P99 was averaging ~920ms while our Redwood runs are seeing ~740-820ms depending on the exact payload. We traced a lot of that to KV cache hit rates and GPU kernel variance for long sequences.
[01:54] Samira: How consistent are those kernel variances? If we bump seq len from 512 to 1024, do we expect a big jump?
[02:02] Marco: Yeah, sequence length matters. For 1024 you see tail increase; our runtime picks different kernels, and that can cause spikes. We can set an autoscale policy or pre-split the workloads to shorter chunks if that helps.
[02:15] Devon: On throughput, CloudX showed better numbers when we used their fp16 path, but you were using a4 q4 — what if we try Redwood fp16?
[02:24] Marco: We can do an fp16 run. Tradeoff is cost and sometimes throughput inconsistency; q4 usually gives better unit cost while keeping latency low.
[02:33] Jordan: Cost is also a big factor. We need to see dollars per 1M tokens for those configs.
[02:38] Claire: We'll add cost-per-million tokens to the CSV. We already have a quick cost model in the sheet but will normalize it to your instance cost assumptions.
[02:46] Samira: Can you remind us how batching is configured in Redwood for the dedicated pool? We want to ensure it's not artificially inflating latency.
[02:54] Marco: Default continuous batching tries to keep latency under the SLO. For the POC we set a max batch wait of 12ms and max batch size 64. We can tighten that to 6ms for lower latency at cost of throughput.
[03:07] Jordan: I think product wants tighter latency for some flows. Could you run a test with batch wait 6ms and batch size 32?
[03:15] Marco: Yep, we can schedule that in the test harness.
[03:19] Devon: Any notes on cold start / model load times? That's another pain for us on CloudX when autoscaling kicks in.
[03:26] Marco: Good question. Cold starts for new containers are ~2.5-4s depending on model size for our dedicated pools, but we have warm pools so it's rarely hit. CloudX reported similar numbers but their autoscale granularity caused more cold starts for bursty traffic.
[03:42] Samira: On models — are you running the same model checkpoint as our baseline? I think CloudX used the open-llm-v2-13b.
[03:50] Claire: We used open-llm-v2-13b-enc on our side to match. There may be slight version diffs; we'll add model hash to the CSV.
[03:58] Jordan: Good. Also security/compliance — our legal team asked if you can provide SOC 2 doc and audit log retention details.
[04:06] Claire: Sure, we'll attach the SOC 2 and the retention policy. For this POC, logs are kept for 90 days by default, and we have options for longer retention in Dedicated/Private.
[04:19] Devon: And SSO? We need SAML for the console.
[04:22] Claire: Yes, we support SAML2 and SCIM provisioning. We'll include the integration steps.
[04:29] Marco: Back to performance — one area where CloudX looked better was sustained throughput at high concurrency. We found they were using larger micro-batch sizes on the GPU which improves throughput but increases median latency. That's where the tradeoff comes in.
[04:44] Samira: Can we get a test that sweeps batch size (16,32,64) and batch wait (6,12,20ms) so we can plot latency vs throughput?
[04:53] Marco: Yep, that's straightforward. We'll push a sweep script to the harness.
[04:57] Claire: Action items — we'll upload the full CSV, a short README with config lines, and the harness link after this call.
[05:05] Jordan: Sounds good. On the VPC/private plan — timeline question. If we decide to move forward, how long to get a private deployment?
[05:13] Marco: For a standard VPC private plane it's 4-6 weeks depending on approvals and infra alignment; on-prem can be longer. We can scope a plan in the next deep dive.
[05:25] Devon: We need details about KMS and HSM integration as well.
[05:29] Claire: We'll include KMS docs. HSM is supported via partner integrations; note that some setups require additional security review.
[05:36] Samira: One nit — the CSV shows a handful of very high outliers on one run (1.6s). Do you have raw traces for that run?
[05:44] Marco: Yes, we kept per-request traces. Looks like a kernel swap on a long sequence combined with a cache miss. We'll annotate the CSV with trace IDs.
[05:53] Jordan: Great. Any other tuning levers you recommend?
[05:57] Marco: KV cache TTL tuning, smarter prefix grouping to increase hit rates, and model quantization profile tuning. Also consider pre-warming for expected bursts.
[06:07] Claire: Recap before we close — Redwood to share CSV & harness (Claire), Marco to run batch sweep + send tuning doc (Marco), Nexus to run the staging test and upload results (Samira/Devon). We'll meet next week same time.
[06:23] Samira: Works for us. Quick question — can you also include the raw logs for the P99 traces?
[06:29] Marco: Yep, will include sanitized logs and trace IDs.
[06:32] Jordan: Thanks everyone. That's it from me.
[06:36] Claire: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the artifacts by tomorrow.

End of transcript.

Notes: Some transcription artifacts (speaker labels, K-V spelling) may be off. Links referenced during call: benchmark spreadsheet (link uploaded to shared drive), test harness (link), SOC2 + security docs (attachments to follow).
